title: The Bread That Is Always There

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And make its plates and dishes of pure gold, as well as its pitchers and bowls for the pouring out of offerings. Put the bread of the Presence on this table to be before me at all times." - Exodus 25:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On this golden table, bread was to sit continually before the Lord — twelve loaves, one for each tribe, replaced week after week without fail. It was called the bread of the Presence. Notice the phrase "at all times." This was not an occasional gesture but an unbroken sign, a constant reminder that God's people were always before Him and always sustained by Him.

Twelve loaves for twelve tribes meant no one was left out. Every tribe, the great and the small, had a place on that table. God's care was not selective; His whole people were continually in His presence. That is a comforting thought for anyone who has ever wondered whether God has overlooked them in the crowd.

And how naturally this leads us to Jesus, who said, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry" (John 6:35). The bread on the table pointed to a deeper hunger than the body's, and to the One who satisfies it. Our souls need feeding daily, not occasionally. If you feel spiritually thin and depleted, come to Him. He is not bread for special occasions; He is the bread that is always there, always enough, always before you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I feeding my soul on Christ regularly, or only occasionally?
Do I believe that I am continually before God, never overlooked?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the bread of life, always available and always enough. Feed my hungry soul on You daily, and thank You that I am continually before the Father. Amen.
